name: Whitefield
tagline: The tech corridor that grew up into a neighbourhood.

image.alt: Glass office towers rising against a blue sky

metro: Purple Line — Whitefield (Kadugodi), Hopefarm, ITPL and Kundalahalli stations
overview: Twenty years ago Whitefield was a cluster of tech parks at the edge of the city. Today it's one of Bengaluru's most complete neighbourhoods: the Purple Line runs to the heart of the city, the international schools are some of the best in the country, and villa communities sit comfortably beside high-rise apartments.
Demand is driven by the tens of thousands who work in ITPL, EPIP and along the Outer Ring Road — which keeps both resale values and rental occupancy steady through market cycles.
pros: Purple Line connects to MG Road and Majestic
cons: Peak-hour traffic on Whitefield Main Road
Groundwater varies by pocket — check water supply
schools: Several IB and IGCSE international schools
CBSE and ICSE schools in every sub-pocket

name: Sarjapur Road
tagline: Schools, space and the best value in the south-east.

image.alt: White minimalist apartment building with clean lines

overview: Sarjapur Road stretches from the Outer Ring Road towards Sarjapur town and has become the default choice for young families who work in the south-east tech belt. The appeal is simple: bigger homes for the money, and a concentration of international schools that few other parts of the city can match.
Infrastructure is catching up. Road widening is under way and a metro corridor has been proposed; until it arrives, homes closer to the Outer Ring Road carry a premium.
pros: More space for the money than central Bengaluru
Large gated communities with full amenities
Close to Outer Ring Road tech parks
cons: Road widening causes congestion near Dommasandra
schools: Six or more international schools within 5 km of Dommasandra
hospitals: Multi-speciality hospitals on the Outer Ring Road and Sarjapur Road

name: Hebbal
tagline: Lakeside living on the road to the airport.

image.alt: Modern residential tower with dark balconies against a clear sky

metro: Hebbal interchange on the airport Blue Line (under construction)
overview: Hebbal sits at the hinge of North Bengaluru — where Bellary Road heads to the airport and the Outer Ring Road loops east to Manyata Tech Park. Its lake, one of the largest in the city, gives the best addresses a permanent view.

With the airport metro line under construction and Manyata continuing to expand, Hebbal has become one of the city's most active luxury markets, with prices now approaching those of central Bengaluru.
pros: Lake views that can't be built out
cons: Hebbal flyover congestion at peak hours
schools: Established schools on Bellary Road and in Sahakar Nagar

name: Devanahalli & Yelahanka
tagline: The airport corridor, and the city's biggest growth story.

image.alt: Contemporary villa with a pool, surrounded by lawns

metro: Airport Blue Line (under construction), with stations along Bellary Road
overview: The stretch from Yelahanka to Devanahalli has changed faster than any part of Bengaluru in the last five years. The airport, the aerospace and IT parks, and new business districts have drawn employers north — and with them, some of the city's best villa and plotted communities.
Land is still available in large parcels here, which means lower densities, more green and prices that are a fraction of central Bengaluru.
pros: Fastest price growth in the last five years
cons: Commute to the south of the city is long
schools: Growing cluster of international schools in Yelahanka and Devanahalli

name: Koramangala
tagline: Start-ups, cafés and some of the city's best-loved streets.

image.alt: Contemporary home with timber cladding and a glass front

metro: No station within the neighbourhood; Yellow Line at BTM Layout and Silk Board
overview: Koramangala is where Bengaluru's start-up story was written — and it still feels like it. Wide, tree-lined blocks of independent houses sit alongside boutique apartment buildings, and the 80 Feet Road and 5th Block have some of the best food in the country.
New supply is scarce, so homes here are bought for the long term and rarely lose value. Rental demand from young professionals is relentless.
best_for: Buyers who want to walk everywhere
pros: Walkable, with the city's best cafés and restaurants
Very low new supply protects values
Central — close to Indiranagar, HSR and the CBD
cons: Flood-prone pockets in heavy rain — check the block
work: Outer Ring Road via Sony Signal

name: Indiranagar
tagline: Old Bengaluru charm with the city's liveliest high street.

image.alt: Dark facade with timber screens, lit warmly at dusk

metro: Purple Line — Indiranagar and Swami Vivekananda Road stations
overview: Indiranagar combines quiet, leafy residential streets with 100 Feet Road and 12th Main — the most vibrant high streets in Bengaluru. It was planned as a residential layout in the 1970s, so plots are generous and roads are wide.
Almost everything that comes up for sale is a resale or a redevelopment, which keeps supply tight and values among the highest in the city.
pros: Best dining and retail in the city
cons: Among the highest prices in Bengaluru
Commercial spillover on some residential streets
schools: Established schools in Indiranagar and HAL 2nd Stage
hospitals: Multi-speciality hospitals on Old Airport Road

name: HSR Layout
tagline: A planned layout with parks on every block.

image.alt: Modern family home with large windows, lit at dusk

metro: HSR Layout station on the Blue Line (under construction); Yellow Line at Silk Board
overview: HSR Layout was planned by the Bangalore Development Authority in the 1980s, and it shows: a regular grid, a park in almost every sector, and 27th Main — one of the city's most popular food streets.
It sits between Koramangala and the Outer Ring Road, so it attracts professionals who want a short commute and families who want parks and schools on their doorstep.
pros: Planned grid with parks in every sector
Next to the Outer Ring Road
cons: Some sectors see waterlogging in heavy rain
schools: Many CBSE and ICSE schools within the layout
hospitals: Multi-speciality hospitals in HSR and on the Outer Ring Road
work: Electronic City via the elevated expressway

name: Electronic City
tagline: The original tech city, now on the Yellow Line.

image.alt: Abstract white architecture with repeating geometric forms

metro: Yellow Line — Electronic City, Konappana Agrahara and Huskur Road stations (operational)
overview: Electronic City was India's first large-scale tech park, and it remains one of the country's biggest employment hubs. The opening of the Yellow Line has transformed the commute into central Bengaluru, and prices have responded.
It remains one of the most affordable parts of the city with direct metro access — which is why rental yields here are among the highest in Bengaluru.
pros: Highest rental yields in our coverage
cons: Hosur Road traffic outside the expressway
schools: CBSE, ICSE and international schools in Phase 1 and on Hosur Road
